correctness.rationale: For n strict ascents the first n digits must be weakly increasing. Equal adjacent digits defer the comparison to the next suffix; at the last digit v, the first different digit in the independent tail must exceed v. Apart from a null set this is also sufficient. The prefix count is binom(n+v-1,n-1) and the tail factor is (b-1-v)/(b-1); summing by two hockey-stick identities gives the frozen formula and its fixed-b asymptotic. At b=2 the same comparison gives A_j=1-D_j almost surely, jointly in j. At b≥3 all-one histories have positive probability and their continuation ratio 1/b+(b-2)/(b(n+2)) strictly varies even beyond any proposed memory order. Independent interval intersections for n=2 give 1/4 and 2/9 at bases 2 and 3; these are spot checks, not the proof. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed. No Lean or expert attestation is inferred.
residual_risks: Classification is for stationary Lebesgue binary adjacent comparisons only, not the full ordinal process or noninteger bases.

value.rationale: There is a sharp qualitative distinction between the iid base-two ordinal observations and infinite memory at every higher integer base, despite iid generating digits in all cases.
